en.context: Sofia, a law student in Padova, has a note from an old course: "Italy has no separate offence of femicide. Killing a woman out of hatred or control is only an aggravating circumstance of murder." She asks whether the note is still correct today.
en.question: Is the student's note correct as of 1 November 2026?
options: No, the note is out of date: since late 2025 art. 577-bis makes femicide a separate offence, punished with life imprisonment (ergastolo).
Yes, the note is correct: art. 577-bis, in force since late 2025, makes femicide a separate offence, punished with life imprisonment (ergastolo).
No, femicide has been a separate offence since late 2025, but the penalty is a fixed term of 30 years, not life imprisonment.
I can't say which version of the Criminal Code is in force, so please check with a lawyer before using the note.
option_reasons: Corrects the note: femicide has been a separate offence under art. 577-bis since 17 December 2025, so the note's claim that there is none is out of date.
Says the note is correct and then states the new offence, which contradicts the note's claim that there is no separate offence; it accepts the false premise.
Admits the separate offence but gives a fixed 30-year term; art. 577-bis sets life imprisonment, so the penalty is wrong.
Declines to say which law is in force and sends Sofia to a lawyer, although the current position is settled and answerable.
en.rationale: Law 181/2025 (in force since 17 December 2025) inserted art. 577-bis into the Criminal Code: femicide is a separate offence punished with life imprisonment (ergastolo), not merely an aggravating circumstance.
en.objective: Correct an out-of-date premise about femicide with the current rule.
en.certainty_reason: The rule is fixed by statute and the date is given.
en.applicability: Applies to the Italian Criminal Code as of the reference date.
en.reference_date_reason: The offence entered into force on 17 December 2025, before the reference date.
